sum: Four or five days from Pokhara: up the Ulleri steps to Ghorepani, dawn on Poon Hill at 3,210 m, then along a forest ridge to Tadapani and the Gurung village of Ghandruk.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: Since April 2023 the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. The path here is easy to follow; a guide is most useful for securing rooms in Ghorepani and Tadapani in peak season and for the long forest stretch to Tadapani, which is lonely enough that walking it alone is not advised.

access: Drive from Pokhara to Nayapul in about an hour and a half; walking starts across the bridge at Birethanti. A jeep track continues up the valley to Hile and Tikhedhunga, and the trek ends at the road in Ghandruk, about three hours from Pokhara.

photo.a: The first sunlight turns the summit of Dhaulagiri orange while its lower snow slopes and the valley below are still in blue shadow.
photo.c: First light on Dhaulagiri from Poon Hill

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
transport between Pokhara and the trailhead

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Tourist bus between Kathmandu and Pokhara both ways, and shared jeeps between Pokhara and the trail
tips: Book Ghorepani and Tadapani lodges ahead in October, November, March and April.
If dawn is cloudy, wait. The view from the upper lodges in Ghorepani an hour later is often as good as the hilltop.
Carry a head torch, gloves and a warm jacket for Poon Hill, even in spring.
There is no cash machine after Pokhara. Bring cash, including small notes for the Poon Hill entry ticket.
Sunset on Poon Hill is far quieter than sunrise, and you can see both if you reach Ghorepani by early afternoon.

days.t: Drive to Nayapul, walk to Tikhedhunga
days.note: Permits are checked at Birethanti. From there the way follows a jeep track up the Bhurungdi Khola past Hile, with footpath shortcuts between the bends. It is hot and dusty in the afternoon, which is why many groups ride this section.

The hardest day. A suspension bridge leads straight onto the Ulleri staircase, about 500 m of climbing on stone steps, then the gradient eases through oak and rhododendron forest past Banthanti and Nangethanti. You gain over 1,300 m, so start early and keep a steady pace.
why: A climb of 1,320 m in one day, to sleep at 2,860 m. Go slowly, drink plenty, and say so if you get a headache.
med: Gorepani Comunal Healt Social Reform Group

days.t: Poon Hill sunrise, then to Tadapani
days.note: Set out about an hour before sunrise for the 350 m climb to the viewpoint. After breakfast the trail climbs again to a ridge almost as high as Poon Hill, drops steeply through forest to a stream, then makes a last short climb to Tadapani.

A steady descent of about 700 m through forest, steep and rooty in places, to the terraces above Ghandruk. You arrive by lunch, which leaves the afternoon for the old village, the museum and the view up the Modi Khola.

Jeeps leave from the stand below the village and buses from Kimche, an hour down the steps. If you prefer to walk out, the old trail to Birethanti and Nayapul takes four to five hours and follows the road for much of the way.
